title: Level 2 Electrical Installation
subtitle: Five copied ElectricianTraining Level 2 mock tests
description: A source-matched Level 2 Electrical Installation exam set copied from the ElectricianTraining mock tests. It adds foundation electrical-science, installation technology, health and safety, cable systems, protection and practical knowledge questions.
format: Five rotating 30-question source mocks. Pass at 60%+ to match the source.

sections.title: ElectricianTraining Level 2 Electrical Installation Mock Exams

questions.prompt: What criteria does an employer have to meet when it becomes a legal requirement to have a written health and safety policy?

options.A: After accident has happened on site
options.C: Under instruction from the local authority
options.D: When employing five or more people

questions.explanation: Employers with five or more employees must record their health and safety policy in writing. Below that threshold the duty to manage safety still exists, but the written policy requirement is not triggered.

questions.prompt: Which regulation requires an employer to ensure a power drill they provide an employee is suitable for use?

options.A: . Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations
options.B: Current edition of the Building Regulations
options.C: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations
options.D: Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations

questions.explanation: PUWER requires equipment provided for work, such as a drill, to be suitable, maintained and safe for the task. It is the regulation aimed directly at work equipment rather than PPE or building standards.

questions.prompt: Which framework covers the legal disposal of waste solvent glue?

options.D: The Health and Safety at Work Act

questions.explanation: Waste solvent glue is classed as hazardous because of its solvent content and environmental risk. The Hazardous Waste Regulations control how that type of waste is stored, transferred and disposed of.

questions.prompt: Which legislation allows local authorities to monitor construction sites to ensure the nuisances such as dust and noise are compliant with agreed limits?

options.D: The Health and Safety at Work Act

questions.explanation: The Control of Pollution Act gives local authorities powers over site nuisances such as noise, dust and other pollution. That is why it is the relevant legislation for agreed site limits.

questions.prompt: What is the immediate action required when a colleague has received a burnt hand when working in a kitchen?

options.B: Place a dry dressing over the wound
options.C: Place the wound under running water

questions.explanation: Cooling a burn under running water removes heat from the tissue and limits further injury. Dressings and help can follow, but cooling is the immediate first-aid action.

questions.prompt: What is the immediate action to be taken when a worker has slipped on site and sustained a back injury?

options.C: Place them in the recovery position
options.D: Try to diagnose the extent of their injuries

questions.explanation: A suspected back injury can involve spinal damage, so the casualty should not be moved unnecessarily. Calling the emergency services gets trained help while avoiding further harm.

questions.prompt: Who must be notified immediately when an operative sustains a back injury from carrying a load?
questions.explanation: The supervisor must be told straight away because they control the work area and accident procedures. They can arrange first aid, reporting and any changes needed to prevent a repeat.

questions.prompt: What are the most common construction site pollutants of water courses and rivers?
questions.explanation: Oil from plant and silt from disturbed ground are common site pollutants that can quickly enter drains and watercourses. Both can cause serious environmental harm even in small quantities.

questions.prompt: What regulations specify the requirements for disposal of low pressure sodium lamps?
questions.explanation: Low pressure sodium lamps are electrical waste and must be handled through the WEEE waste stream. WEEE rules ensure lamps and their hazardous contents are recovered or disposed of correctly.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to report asbestos immediately if it is suspected as being present?

options.B: To ensure the job is not held up

questions.explanation: Suspected asbestos must be reported immediately to stop fibres being disturbed and inhaled. The key safety aim is preventing unnecessary exposure before the material is assessed.

questions.prompt: What action is required when a work process is risk assessed as 'High' risk?

options.A: Continue working and complete corrective actions within a month
options.B: Continue working and complete corrective actions within a week
options.C: Stop the activity immediately and complete set actions
options.D: Stop the activity within a week and complete set actions

questions.explanation: A high-risk activity should be stopped until the required controls are put in place. Continuing before the actions are complete leaves workers exposed to a known serious risk.

questions.prompt: What is the most appropriate action to reduce the risk of harm to workers when damaged asbestos is encountered in a building?

options.A: Have the asbestos professionally removed immediately
options.B: Issue all workers with dust masks and safety glasses
options.C: Use barriers around the area in the building effected
options.D: Use sheeting to cover the localised damaged area

questions.explanation: Damaged asbestos can release dangerous fibres, so it should be dealt with by competent licensed specialists. Simple barriers or ordinary dust masks do not make the material safe.

questions.prompt: What item of PPE must be used when drilling a hole in a steel wall bracket using a pillar drill?
questions.explanation: Drilling steel can throw swarf and sharp particles from the workpiece. Safety goggles protect the eyes from that immediate mechanical hazard.

questions.prompt: What must the first aid provision for a construction site reflect?
questions.explanation: First-aid provision must match the hazards and likely injuries on the site. A construction site with higher-risk work needs provision based on what could realistically happen, not just headcount.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to replace first aid supplies each time they are used?

options.C: To ensure accidents can be effectively prevented
options.D: To ensure resources are always available in case of accidents

questions.explanation: Used first-aid supplies must be replaced so treatment is available for the next incident. An incomplete kit can delay basic care when an accident occurs.

questions.prompt: What certification defines an operative's competence to erect a mobile scaffold tower?
questions.explanation: PASMA training is the recognised competence route for assembling and using mobile access towers. It shows the operative has been trained in safe tower erection and inspection.

questions.prompt: What is the main risk to an electrician when safe isolation is not carried out on a live circuit being worked on?

options.A: Electric shock caused by direct contact
options.B: Electric shock caused by static discharge
options.C: Electrical shock caused by electromagnetic interference
options.D: Electrical shock caused by indirect contact

questions.explanation: Without safe isolation, the electrician may touch live parts directly. Direct contact with live conductors is the immediate electric shock hazard.

questions.prompt: What type of hazardous substance is classified by the label shown in the image?
questions.explanation: The flame-over-circle hazard symbol identifies an oxidising substance. Oxidisers can intensify fire because they release or support oxygen in a reaction.

questions.prompt: What health and safety term defines the potential exposure of a worker to loud noise?
questions.explanation: A hazard is something with the potential to cause harm. Loud noise is a hazard because exposure can damage hearing.

questions.prompt: What is the specific hazard when cables are run in thermal insulation?
questions.explanation: Thermal insulation prevents heat from escaping from cables, so the cable can run hotter than designed. Excess heat can damage insulation and create a fire risk.

questions.prompt: What term defines the situation where an electrician is working at height off a ladder?
questions.explanation: Working from a ladder is a hazard because it creates the potential for a fall from height. The risk level then depends on factors such as height, duration and control measures.

questions.prompt: What practice is employed to address the potential hazard of electrical shock from trailing leads for power tools on construction sites?

options.A: Use of 110 V centre tapped supplies
options.B: Use of 230 V single phase supplies
options.C: Use of 400 V three phase supplies
options.D: Use of 500 V DC single phase supplies

questions.explanation: A 110 V centre-tapped supply limits the voltage to earth to about 55 V on each conductor. That reduces the severity of shock from damaged trailing leads on construction sites.

questions.prompt: Which type of fire extinguisher is best suited for use on live electrical fires?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is non-conductive and leaves no residue, so it is suitable for many live electrical fires. Water and wet chemical extinguishers can introduce shock and damage risks.

questions.prompt: Which building component is most likely to contain asbestos?
questions.explanation: Older cisterns and water tanks were sometimes made from asbestos-cement materials. The other listed items are less typical asbestos-containing components in this context.

questions.prompt: What is the first action that must be taken when suspected asbestos is identified during refurbishment work of a dwelling?

options.B: Remove the affected area and place in bags
options.C: Seal the suspected material with paint

questions.explanation: The first action is to stop work so the suspected asbestos is not disturbed further. Assessment and specialist controls can then be arranged before anyone continues.

questions.prompt: The standard distribution voltage to light industry is:
questions.explanation: 11 kV is a common distribution voltage used to supply light industrial sites before transformation to low voltage. The higher values are transmission or sub-transmission levels rather than typical light-industry distribution.

questions.prompt: A typical insulator for an overhead line transmission system would be:
questions.explanation: Glass and porcelain have high electrical resistance and withstand outdoor weathering. That makes them suitable insulators for overhead line supports.

questions.prompt: By law electricity nominal supply voltages must be kept within:
questions.explanation: UK nominal low-voltage supplies are permitted to vary within +10% and -6% of the declared voltage. This tolerance allows normal network variation while keeping equipment within its design range.

questions.prompt: Which of the following systems has no moving parts:
questions.explanation: Photovoltaic systems convert light directly into electricity in semiconductor cells. They do not need turbines, pumps or other moving mechanical parts.

questions.prompt: What is the term for a number of Solar PV modules connected in series:
questions.explanation: Solar PV modules connected in series form a string. Series connection raises the voltage while the same current flows through each module.

questions.prompt: Maternity rights are covered under which of the following Acts:
questions.explanation: Maternity rights are employment protections, so they sit under employment law. The Employment Rights Act is the relevant Act among the options.

questions.prompt: The prevention of disease is part of the responsibility of which of the following construction site visitors:
questions.explanation: A water inspector is concerned with the safety of water supplies and prevention of contamination. That role links directly to disease prevention through water hygiene.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would not normally come under the umbrella of company policy and procedures:
questions.explanation: Statutory cancellation rights are legal consumer rights, not an internal company rule. Policies such as dress code and timekeeping are normally set by the company.

questions.prompt: The term given to the person responsible for an electrical system is the:
questions.explanation: The duty holder is the person or organisation responsible for the electrical system and its safety. The term is used for the person who must ensure duties are met.

questions.prompt: Specific guidance on carrying out work on electrical systems is given in the:

options.C: Health and Safety at Work Act

questions.explanation: The IET Wiring Regulations give the detailed technical requirements for electrical installation work. They are the practical reference for how electrical systems should be designed, installed and verified.

questions.prompt: Which of the following people would be responsible for creating working drawings from an idea or scheme submitted by the client:
questions.explanation: A design engineer turns a client brief or scheme into workable technical drawings. That role converts the idea into information installers can build from.

questions.prompt: Which organisation acts as a means of a co-ordinator between unions and employers with respect to grading and rates of pay for employees:
questions.explanation: The JIB provides industry arrangements for grading, employment conditions and rates of pay in electrical contracting. It acts as the link between employers and labour interests.

questions.prompt: The first thing to be considered when planning a new installation is the:

options.C: List of materials to be used

questions.explanation: Planning starts with what the client needs the installation to do. Cost, labour and materials can only be properly decided once the client brief is understood.

questions.prompt: The person who oversees a number of workers on a variety of sites would normally be the:
questions.explanation: A works manager usually has responsibility across multiple jobs or sites. A site foreman normally supervises day-to-day work on one site.

questions.prompt: The role of a contracts manager working for an electrical contracting company is to:

options.A: Check the profits of the main contractor
options.B: Deliver materials to the contract site
options.D: Take charge of all contractors on a site

questions.explanation: A contracts manager coordinates resources, progress and communication so contract deadlines are achieved. They manage delivery rather than taking charge of every contractor on site.

questions.prompt: The person required to check the quality of the site materials and equipment against the specification and drawings, is:
questions.explanation: The clerk of works checks that site materials and workmanship match the drawings and specification. Their role is quality inspection on behalf of the client or project team.

questions.prompt: A nominated supplier might be selected by:

options.B: The foreman or clerk of works

questions.explanation: A nominated supplier is named for procurement within the contract arrangements. The main contractor or subcontractor may select or use that supplier to obtain specified goods.

questions.prompt: The area of control relating to air conditioning systems is that of the:
questions.explanation: A building management system monitors and controls building services such as heating, ventilation and air conditioning. Air-conditioning control is therefore part of the BMS area.

questions.prompt: The IET Regulations state requirements intended to provide:
questions.explanation: The primary purpose of the IET Regulations is safety, especially protection of persons from electric shock, burns and fire. Economy or detailed instructions for every case are not their main aim.

questions.prompt: Particular standards or Codes of Practice would most likely be referred to when dealing with:
questions.explanation: Codes of Practice are used where extra guidance is needed for particular risks or specialist areas. They supplement general rules for areas of particular concern.

questions.prompt: The right to a fair trial is covered under which of the following Acts:
questions.explanation: The Human Rights Act incorporates rights such as the right to a fair trial. The other Acts listed cover different employment or data matters.

questions.prompt: It is necessary to record materials received and used on site in order to:

options.A: Check the price of the contract
options.C: Maintain stocks and check materials used

questions.explanation: Recording materials received and used lets the site maintain stock control and compare use against the job allowance. It also helps identify shortages or wastage early.

questions.prompt: The preferred method of instructing the client in the correct use and maintenance of electrical equipment used within an installation would be to:

options.A: Leave relevant manufacturer's literature adjacent to equipment
options.B: Provide them with a guided tour and verbal instructions during the handover period
options.C: Provide them with an operations and maintenance manual
options.D: Provide them with the manufacturer's catalogue

questions.explanation: An operations and maintenance manual gives the client the correct operating instructions, maintenance information and key documents in one place. Verbal guidance or loose catalogues are less reliable for handover.

questions.prompt: A room of width 2.6m is to be represented on a drawing with a scale of 1:50. What length would this appear as on the drawing in:
questions.explanation: At a 1:50 scale, the drawing length is the real length divided by 50. 2.6 m divided by 50 is 0.052 m, which is 5.2 cm.

questions.prompt: The type of drawing which could be used as part of a record of work done is an:
questions.explanation: An as-fitted drawing records how the installation was actually completed. It is used after the work as a record for future maintenance or alteration.

questions.prompt: The main purpose of an assembly diagram is

options.A: Show how the components fit together
options.B: To provide different views of the components
options.C: To show the sequence of control
options.D: Use symbols to represent circuit components and show their connections

questions.explanation: An assembly diagram shows the physical relationship of parts and how they fit together. It is about assembly rather than circuit operation.

questions.prompt: Another description for a tender document is:
questions.explanation: A tender is a bid to carry out work for a stated price or terms. It is the contractor's offer in response to the client's documents.

questions.prompt: The two key pieces of information required when completing a day work sheet are:

options.A: Any special conditions and work carried out
options.B: The amount of extra time and materials that have been used
options.C: The name and employee number of the electrician
options.D: The name of the authorizing person and their signature

questions.explanation: Daywork sheets record extra labour time and materials used outside the original measured work. Those details allow the additional work to be valued and agreed.

questions.prompt: A contract document is an assurance that:

options.A: Good site management will be guaranteed
options.B: Labour on site can be specially programmed
options.C: The building owner and contractor will work together
options.D: The work and the payment will be carried out

questions.explanation: A contract document records the agreement that the contractor will carry out the work and the client will pay for it. It creates obligations on both sides.

questions.prompt: A means of displaying work activities against time can be accomplished by the use of a:
questions.explanation: A bar chart, often a programme chart, shows activities laid out against time. This makes it easy to see when each task is planned to start and finish.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would you not expect to find on a Material List:
questions.explanation: A material list normally identifies items, descriptions and quantities needed for the job. The detailed technical specification is usually held in the specification document rather than the list itself.

questions.prompt: The main contractor involved with a large project is most likely to be a:
questions.explanation: On a large building project the main contractor is usually a builder who coordinates the overall construction work. Specialist trades such as electricians commonly work as subcontractors.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would not be found in an operational manual:

options.A: A description of how the system is to operate

questions.explanation: An operation manual explains how to use and maintain the installed equipment. Manufacturers' costs are commercial information and are not normally part of the handover manual.

questions.prompt: A diagram which takes into account the physical outline and connections of the circuit would be a:
questions.explanation: A wiring diagram shows the physical wiring connections and how conductors terminate on equipment. It is more connection-focused than a purely logical schematic.

questions.prompt: What does the Health and Safety Executive inspect?

options.A: Companies for compliance with health and safety standards
options.D: Work completed on a construction site

questions.explanation: The HSE checks that work is being planned and controlled safely, including risk assessments before work begins. Those assessments show hazards have been considered and managed.

questions.prompt: Personal information related to business involving credit reference agencies is protected under which of the following Acts:
questions.explanation: The Data Protection Act protects personal information held or used by organisations. Credit reference information is personal data and must be handled lawfully.

questions.prompt: Probably the most efficient and fastest means of communicating technical information would be by:
questions.explanation: Email is fast, creates a written record and can carry drawings or technical attachments. That makes it an efficient way to communicate technical information.

questions.prompt: An architect wishing particular design expertise would probably employ:
questions.explanation: Consulting engineers are brought in for specialist design knowledge. An architect would use them when a project needs technical engineering expertise beyond architectural design.

questions.prompt: The Electricity at Work Regulations applies to:
questions.explanation: The Electricity at Work Regulations apply broadly to electrical systems, equipment and work activities. They are not limited to one type of installation or premises.

questions.prompt: For which of the following locations would you expect to have to refer to a specific Code of Practice:
questions.explanation: Emergency lighting and alarm systems are safety systems with dedicated standards and Codes of Practice. Their design and testing need more specific guidance than ordinary final circuits.

questions.prompt: Which of the following frequencies are covered in the IET Wiring Regulations:
questions.explanation: The IET Wiring Regulations cover common AC supply frequencies used in installations, including 50 Hz, 60 Hz and 400 Hz within their scope. These frequencies appear in normal mains and specialist supplies.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would you expect to find in a specification:

options.C: The amount of items to be used

questions.explanation: A specification states what the client requires and the standards the finished work must meet. It becomes the technical brief for pricing and installation.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would you not find in an operations manual:

options.A: A copy of the IET Regulations
options.B: A description of how the system is to operate
options.D: Manufacturers technical data for all major components

questions.explanation: An operations manual is installation-specific handover information. A full copy of the IET Regulations is a general reference book, not part of the operating instructions for one installation.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following procedures should a contracting electrician working on a site use for receiving materials, tools and equipment:

options.C: Inform the supervisor when next seen

questions.explanation: Delivery notes should be checked and retained to prove what materials, tools and equipment arrived on site. This supports stock control and resolves later disputes.

questions.prompt: What document details - extra work- carried out that was not on the original contract:
questions.explanation: A daywork sheet records extra work carried out outside the original contract. It captures the additional labour and materials so they can be agreed and paid for.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would not normally be placed on a Materials List:
questions.explanation: A materials list is normally about what items are needed and in what quantities. Delivery dates are part of ordering or delivery paperwork rather than the core material list.

questions.prompt: A nominated subcontractor might be chosen by:

options.A: The client, main contractor or architect
options.B: The foreman or clerk of works

questions.explanation: A nominated subcontractor may be selected by the client, main contractor or architect because they want a particular specialist used. The nomination then becomes part of the contract arrangements.

questions.prompt: Material delivered to site should be checked against the delivery note and the:
questions.explanation: Materials delivered to site should match both the delivery note and the original order. Checking against the order confirms the right goods were supplied, not just what the delivery note says.

questions.prompt: What is the typical sequence of events leading to contract work with the following steps:- 1 Order 2 Contract 3 Tender 4 Specification:
questions.explanation: The usual sequence is specification, tender, order, then contract. The client defines the work first, contractors price it, the client orders it, and the formal agreement follows.

questions.prompt: To check the ongoing progress of a contract, the contracts manager would use:
questions.explanation: Worksheets and time sheets show what labour has been used and what work has been completed. A contracts manager can compare them with the programme to monitor progress.

questions.prompt: Access to goods and services is covered under which of the following Acts:
questions.explanation: Access to goods and services was covered by disability discrimination legislation in this source context. The principle is that disabled people must not be unfairly denied access.

questions.prompt: A means of displaying work activities against time can be accomplished by the use of a:
questions.explanation: A bar chart displays activities against a time scale. It is a simple way to plan and track when work stages should happen.

questions.prompt: If a cable run measured on a drawing with a scale of 1:25 is 65 cm, what is the actual length of the cable run:
questions.explanation: At 1:25 scale, 65 cm on the drawing represents 65 x 25 cm in reality. That is 1625 cm, or 16.25 m.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is used as a symbol to denote a:
questions.explanation: On installation drawings, a rectangle can be used as the symbol for a consumer unit or distribution equipment. Symbols let drawings show equipment positions without drawing the real object.

questions.prompt: A room measures 4.25 metres long, what would it measure on a drawing scaled at 1:20:
questions.explanation: At 1:20 scale, the drawing length is the real length divided by 20. 4.25 m becomes 0.2125 m, which is 21.25 cm.

questions.prompt: Which of the following uses symbols to represent all circuit components and shows how these are connected by following a logical progression from supply to output:
questions.explanation: A schematic diagram uses symbols and a logical flow from supply to output. It explains how the circuit works rather than exactly where every item is physically installed.

questions.prompt: Which of the following diagrams would you not use to work on a new installation:
questions.explanation: An as-built wiring diagram records what was installed after completion. New work is carried out from design, layout or working drawings instead.

questions.prompt: A bill of quantities is a:
questions.explanation: A bill of quantities supports tendering by listing measured work and quantities for contractors to price. It gives each tenderer the same basis for the bid.

questions.prompt: In Situ measurements are obtained by:

options.B: Measuring actual values in position on site

questions.explanation: In situ measurements are taken with the item in its actual position on site. This avoids relying only on drawings or assumed dimensions.

questions.prompt: A statutory regulation means that it has been:
questions.explanation: A statutory regulation has legal force because it is made or agreed by law. It must be complied with, unlike purely advisory guidance.

questions.prompt: BS EN numbers on electrical equipment applies to:
questions.explanation: BS EN markings show that a British Standard is aligned with a European harmonised standard. They indicate equipment has been assessed against that shared standard.

questions.prompt: When a regulation is termed - absolute - then that regulation:

options.A: Must be met regardless of costs
options.B: Must be met within an agreed time
options.C: Must be met within reasonable costs

questions.explanation: An absolute duty must be met regardless of cost, time or inconvenience. It is stronger than duties qualified by what is reasonably practicable.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not an liP basic principle:

options.A: A commitment from the senior level of the organisation to develop all employees
options.B: Evaluate the outcomes of training and development as a basis for continuous improvement
options.C: Gathering of knowledge and experience through self motivation
options.D: Regular reviews of training and development of employees

questions.explanation: Investors in People focuses on planned organisational commitment to training, development and improvement. Informal self-motivated knowledge gathering is not one of its basic principles.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would not be a benefit for an organisation being ISO 9000 certificated:

options.A: Equality of pay between men and women

questions.explanation: ISO 9000 is a quality management certification, so its benefits relate to consistent processes and customer confidence. Equal pay is an employment-rights issue, not a quality-system benefit.

questions.prompt: With regards to the design of the water, central heating, air conditioning and electrical services on a large construction project, who is the person responsible?
questions.explanation: A building services engineer coordinates technical services such as water, heating, air conditioning and electrical systems. That role covers the integrated services design on large projects.

questions.prompt: Which statutory regulations lay down the measures which must be taken to ensure the safe installation and use of electrical equipment:
questions.explanation: The Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 are statutory duties for preventing danger from electrical systems at work. They cover safe installation, maintenance and use of electrical equipment.

questions.prompt: What is the most appropriate action for an HSE inspector to take after discovering some defective lights within an emergency lighting system:
questions.explanation: An improvement notice is used where a defect needs correcting but does not require immediate prohibition of work. Defective emergency lighting can be formally required to be improved within a set period.

questions.prompt: A diagram showing all conductors and the connection of electrical components is called a:
questions.explanation: A circuit diagram shows the conductors and how electrical components are connected. It represents the circuit relationships rather than the physical route on site.

questions.prompt: A location drawing is scaled at 1:50. The route length of a cable run on the drawing is 85mm the length of the cable will be:
questions.explanation: At a 1:50 scale, 85 mm on the drawing represents 85 x 50 mm in reality. That equals 4250 mm, or 4.25 m.

questions.prompt: The preferred method of instructing the client in the correct use and maintenance of electrical equipment used within an installation would be to:

options.A: Leave relevant manufacturer's literature adjacent to equipment
options.B: Provide them with a guided tour and verbal instructions during the handover period
options.C: Provide them with an operations and maintenance manual
options.D: Provide them with the manufacturer's catalogue

questions.explanation: An operations and maintenance manual gives the client durable instructions for safe use, maintenance and future reference. It is better than relying on a verbal handover alone.

questions.prompt: The requirements for overload current protection are fulfilled when:
questions.explanation: Overload protection is correctly coordinated when Ib is no greater than In and In is no greater than Iz. Only 10 A <= 15 A <= 18 A satisfies that sequence.

questions.prompt: A heater taking 40A is supplied by a cable 10m long. If the cable has a volt drop of 4mV per ampere per metre, the voltage drop in the cable will be:
questions.explanation: Voltage drop is calculated as mV per amp per metre times current times length, divided by 1000. 4 x 40 x 10 / 1000 = 1.6 V.

questions.prompt: Which domestic accessory would you expect to have terminals labelled, N, Loop and S/L:
questions.explanation: A ceiling rose commonly has neutral, permanent loop and switched-line terminals. The S/L terminal feeds the lamp only when the switch is closed.

questions.prompt: A Motor is connected via a flexible conduit to a starter. The continuity of the protective conductor is maintained by:

options.B: The flexible conduit provided the conduit boxes are scraped and locknuts are used
options.C: The flexible conduit without any further modification

questions.explanation: Flexible conduit should not be relied on as the protective conductor for a motor connection. A separate circuit protective conductor maintains a dependable earth path despite movement and vibration.

questions.prompt: Cables not likely to be affected by electrical interference are:
questions.explanation: Fibre-optic cable transmits light rather than electrical signals. Because it contains no metallic signal path, it is not normally affected by electromagnetic interference.

questions.prompt: Fire alarm sounders must be capable of producing a minimum of:
questions.explanation: General fire alarm sounders are expected to achieve at least 65 dB in many occupied areas. This ensures the alarm is audible above normal background noise.

questions.prompt: What is the efficiency of a 172.5 Watt domestic heater which draws 2 A from the domestic supply:
questions.explanation: Input power is voltage times current, so 230 V x 2 A = 460 W. Efficiency is output divided by input, so 172.5 / 460 = 37.5%.

questions.prompt: The effect of improving the power factor of a fluorescent lamp circuit is that the current taken from the supply is:

options.B: Lagging the supply voltage by a larger angle

questions.explanation: Improving power factor reduces the reactive current needed for the same useful power. The supply current therefore becomes smaller.

questions.prompt: In agricultural premises an rcd may be used for protection against fire providing the operating current does not exceed:
questions.explanation: For fire protection in agricultural premises, an RCD operating current not exceeding 300 mA may be used. This level helps detect leakage that could overheat or ignite materials.

questions.prompt: The internal area of a cable delivery system, to avoid internal sealing, must not be greater than:
questions.explanation: 710 mm² is the threshold used here before extra internal sealing considerations apply to the cable delivery system. Keeping within it avoids the need for that additional sealing requirement.

questions.prompt: Copper links are used across joints in metallic trunking installations in order to:

options.A: Increase the strength of the joint
options.B: Maintain the electrical continuity of the exposed conductive parts
options.C: Provide a temporary fixing before the main bolts are fitted

questions.explanation: Metallic trunking joints must maintain electrical continuity so exposed metal remains connected to earth. Copper links bridge joints that might otherwise become high resistance.

questions.prompt: The purpose of segregated trunking is to:

options.A: Allow accommodation of circuits having different voltage bands
options.B: Prevent overheating in vertical trunking runs
options.C: Prevent the spread of fire within the trunking
options.D: Support the cables installed in the trunking

questions.explanation: Segregated trunking separates circuits of different voltage bands or services. This reduces interference and prevents unsafe contact between incompatible circuits.

questions.prompt: PME (Protective Multiple Earthing) is mainly associated with which system of earthing:
questions.explanation: PME uses a combined protective earth and neutral in the supply that is separated at the installation. That arrangement is the TN-C-S earthing system.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a method of protection from direct contact (basic protection):
questions.explanation: Automatic disconnection of supply is a fault-protection measure, not basic protection against direct contact. Basic protection uses insulation, barriers, enclosures or placing live parts out of reach.

questions.prompt: Supplementary bonding conductors without mechanical protection used to connect water pipes supplying a sink unit should be at least:
questions.explanation: A supplementary bonding conductor without mechanical protection needs a larger minimum size for durability. The required minimum in this case is 4.0 mm² copper.

questions.prompt: When a person receives a shock by touching a metallic part not normally live but made live under fault conditions is said to be in:
questions.explanation: Indirect contact means touching an exposed conductive part that has become live because of a fault. It differs from direct contact with a live conductor itself.

questions.prompt: Where a firefighter's switch is to be installed, in order to comply with BS 7671 it must be:

options.A: No more than 2.75 m from the ground with the off position at the bottom
options.B: No more than 2.75 m from the ground with the off position at the top
options.C: No more than 3.75 m from the ground with the off position at the bottom
options.D: No more than 3.75 m from the ground with the off position at the top

questions.explanation: A firefighter's switch must be accessible and arranged so the off position is at the top, with the height limited to 2.75 m. This makes emergency operation clear and practical.

questions.prompt: Circuit protective conductors are connected between:

options.B: The main earth terminal and exposed conductive parts
options.C: The main earth terminal and extraneous conductive parts
options.D: The main earth terminal and the earth rod

questions.explanation: Circuit protective conductors connect exposed conductive parts back to the main earth terminal. That provides the fault-current path needed for protective devices to operate.

questions.prompt: Which of the following protective devices is used in domestic plug tops:
questions.explanation: Domestic plug tops use BS 1362 cartridge fuses. These fuses protect the flexible cord connected to the plug.

questions.prompt: Fusing factor is the ratio of:
questions.explanation: Fusing factor compares the current needed to melt the fuse with the fuse current rating. It is therefore fusing current divided by current rating.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the National Grid:

options.A: Transmission of electricity from power stations to factories
options.B: Transmission of electricity from power stations to industrial locations
options.C: Transmission of electricity from power stations to substations
options.D: Transmission of electricity from sub stations to domestic premises

questions.explanation: The National Grid transmits electricity in bulk from power stations to substations. Local distribution networks then take it onward to consumers.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following types of power stations does not use a fossil fuel to generate electricity:
questions.explanation: Nuclear power stations use nuclear fission as the heat source rather than burning coal, gas or oil. That is why they are not fossil-fuel power stations.

questions.prompt: Increasing the excitation of an a.c. generator will cause the:
questions.explanation: Increasing excitation strengthens the generator's magnetic field. A stronger field induces a higher output voltage.

questions.prompt: Which of the following systems require large amounts of water for operation:
questions.explanation: Micro-hydro generation depends on moving water to drive a turbine. It therefore requires a suitable water flow and head to operate.

questions.prompt: Which of the following systems require separate pipework, storage and a filtration system for operation:
questions.explanation: Grey water recycling needs separate pipework to collect used water, plus storage and filtration before reuse. It is a plumbing and treatment system rather than an electricity generator.

questions.prompt: A statutory regulation means that it has been:
questions.explanation: A statutory regulation has force because it is made by law. Compliance is therefore a legal requirement, not just good practice.

questions.prompt: When a regulation is termed - absolute- then that regulation:

options.B: Must be met regardless of costs
options.C: Must be met within an agreed time
options.D: Requires a competent electrician to complete

questions.explanation: An absolute duty must be complied with regardless of cost or difficulty. It is not balanced against what is reasonably practicable.

questions.prompt: Which of the following documents is not produced by the client:
questions.explanation: A tender is produced by a contractor as an offer to carry out the work. The client normally produces documents such as the order, specification or variation order.

questions.prompt: A room measures 4.25 metres long, what would it measure on a drawing scaled at 1:20:
questions.explanation: At a 1:20 scale, 4.25 m is divided by 20 for the drawing length. The result is 0.2125 m, or 21.25 cm.

questions.prompt: The main purpose of an assembly diagram is:

options.A: Show how the components fit together
options.B: To provide different views of the components
options.C: To show the sequence of control
options.D: Use symbols to represent circuit components and show their connections

questions.explanation: An assembly diagram shows how separate parts are put together. It is used to understand the physical assembly rather than the circuit logic.

questions.prompt: What is the fault current required for a disconnection time of 0.1 second for a BS EN 60898 Type B 6A protection device as stated in BS 7671:
questions.explanation: A Type B BS EN 60898 device trips instantaneously at around 3 to 5 times its rating. For a 6 A device, 5 x 6 A gives the 30 A fault current used for the stated disconnection time.

questions.prompt: In the equation S = √I2 x t/k what does the symbol 'I' signify::

options.B: The maximum demand current of the installation
options.C: Current rating of the protective device

questions.explanation: In the adiabatic equation, I is the prospective fault current through the protective conductor. That current, together with time, determines the conductor size needed to withstand fault energy.

questions.prompt: A warning notice must be fixed to all:

options.B: Electric motors having a rating exceeding 0.37 kW
options.C: Equipment operating in excess of 230V and where such voltage would not normally be expected
options.D: Switchgear which cannot normally be observed by the operator

questions.explanation: A warning notice is needed where equipment operates above 230 V in a place where that voltage would not normally be expected. The warning reduces the chance of accidental contact or wrong assumptions.

questions.prompt: Non-metallic conduit must only be used within suitable ranges of:
questions.explanation: Non-metallic conduit can soften, become brittle or lose strength outside its temperature rating. Ambient temperature is therefore a key suitability limit.

questions.prompt: Highest frequency data transmission rates can be achieved by the use of:
questions.explanation: Fibre-optic systems carry data as light pulses and support very high bandwidth. They also avoid the frequency limitations of metallic data cables.

questions.prompt: Escape lighting is required to operate for between:
questions.explanation: Escape lighting must keep routes visible for a specified duration, commonly within the 1 to 3 hour range depending on the premises. That duration supports safe evacuation and re-entry decisions.

questions.prompt: Direct acting space heaters:

options.B: Give out heat at a steady rate

questions.explanation: Direct acting space heaters produce heat as soon as they are energised. They respond quickly to temperature changes rather than storing heat for later release.

questions.prompt: Efficacy is a measure of a lighting systems:
questions.explanation: Lighting efficacy compares useful light output with electrical input power. In practice it is expressed as lumens per watt, so higher efficacy means more light for the same energy.

questions.prompt: Protection against objects greater than 1mm diameter has an IP classification of:
questions.explanation: The first digit 4 in IP4X means protection against solid objects greater than 1 mm. The X means no water-protection rating is being stated.

questions.prompt: The space factor for cables in trunking should not exceed:
questions.explanation: Trunking must not be overfilled because heat dissipation and cable installation become difficult. The accepted maximum space factor here is 45%.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are standard sizes of conduit:
questions.explanation: 16 mm, 20 mm and 25 mm are standard conduit sizes. The other options include non-standard sizes for this context.

questions.prompt: Inspection type conduit accessories are used to:

options.B: Facilitate the drawing in of cables into the conduit

questions.explanation: Inspection conduit fittings provide access points that help cables be drawn into the conduit. They also allow inspection of the draw-in route.

questions.prompt: The recommended wiring system use for use on a dairy farm is:
questions.explanation: Dairy farms are corrosive and regularly washed down, so stainless steel withstands moisture and chemical attack better than ordinary steel or PVC. It is the robust wiring system choice.

questions.prompt: The earthed neutral of the authorities supply must be fitted at the intake position with a:
questions.explanation: The supply neutral must not be fused or interrupted by a single-pole switch at the intake. A solid link maintains the required neutral connection.

questions.prompt: The main purpose of equipotential bonding is to:

options.B: Increase the impedance of the earth return
options.C: Maintain adjacent metalwork at the same electrical potential

questions.explanation: Equipotential bonding connects metalwork so exposed and extraneous conductive parts remain at substantially the same potential. This reduces touch voltage under fault conditions.

questions.prompt: If a main equipotential bonding conductor is connected to a gas pipe, the connection must be made within:

options.A: 300mm of the meter on the consumers side
options.B: 300mm of the meter on the supply side
options.C: 600mm of the meter on the consumer's side
options.D: 600mm of the meter on the supply side

questions.explanation: Main bonding to a gas pipe is made within 600 mm of the meter on the consumer's side, before branch pipework where practicable. This bonds the incoming service close to where it enters the installation.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum earth fault loop impedance outside the consumers installation for a TN-S system:
questions.explanation: For a TN-S supply, the typical maximum external earth fault loop impedance value is 0.8 ohms. This is the distributor's earth path outside the consumer's installation.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 allows a number of devices to be used as isolators. One device which can NOT be used for this purpose is:
questions.explanation: A semiconductor device does not provide the reliable physical separation required for isolation. Isolators need dependable contact separation that can be secured and verified.

questions.prompt: Which of the following types of RCD has is the general standard with no time delay built in:
questions.explanation: The general RCD type has no intentional time delay, unlike selective time-delayed devices. The source labels that no-delay option as O Type.

questions.prompt: Which of the following circuit breakers would be most suitable for use with circuits feeding large transformers:
questions.explanation: Type D circuit breakers tolerate high inrush currents before magnetic tripping. Large transformers can draw heavy magnetising inrush, so Type D is the suitable curve.

questions.prompt: The standard distribution voltage to light industry is:
questions.explanation: 11 kV is a normal distribution voltage for supplying light industrial installations before local transformation. It is lower than transmission voltages such as 132 kV or 400 kV.

questions.prompt: A typical insulator for an overhead line transmission system would be:
questions.explanation: Overhead-line insulators must support the conductor while resisting current flow and weathering. Glass and porcelain have high electrical resistance and good outdoor durability, which is why they are typical choices.

questions.prompt: By law electricity nominal supply voltages must be kept within:
questions.explanation: The permitted nominal supply voltage range is +10% and -6%. That tolerance allows network variation while keeping equipment supplied within acceptable limits.

questions.prompt: Which of the following systems has no moving parts:
questions.explanation: Photovoltaic panels generate electricity directly from light and have no rotating machine. Wind and hydro systems require moving mechanical parts.

questions.prompt: What is the term for a number of Solar PV modules connected in series:
questions.explanation: A series-connected group of PV modules is called a string. Adding modules in series increases the string voltage.
